2. Application -This line output transformer is meant to provide the required scanning amplitude for 470 mm, 510 mm, 590 mm and 610 mm TV picture tubes in television receivers presenting 625 lines at 50 frames per second. It is intended for use in conjunction with: a) deflection b) linearity Typical coil unit DCU lH, and control unit LCU IH. schematic diagram is shown In Fig. 1.

3. Description - The line output transformer shall have primary, secondary, auxiliary and EHT The transformer windings wound on a ferrite core with suitable resin impregnation/encapsulation. shall meet the self extinguishing and non-dripping requirements of IS : 616-1981 `Safety requirements for mains operated electronic and related apparatus for household and similar general use ( first revision 1'. 4. Mounting -The line output transformer shall be provided with four mounting pins and two threaded holes for mounting. The line output transformer may be mounted on either a printed wiring board or a metal chassis as detailed in Fig. 3.

The line output

transformer

should

not be left floating

but must be connected

to the chassis,

The operation of the line output transformer is Influenced by its surroundings, variations in electrical characteristics due to the influence of the surrounding components, shields and circuitry can be compensated to a certain degree by selecting the right value of the capacitor c4. The deflection unit is connected to the secondary which is separated from the primary by the booster capacitor C7. Pulses for blanking, synchronization, etc, are to be taken directly from the deflection unit connections. A ciruit diagram of a flywheel synchronization is given in Fig. 4. The split secondary offer possibilities of alternate connections as detailed in Fig. 4. The conventional circuit is .obtained with booster capacitor C-7-56nF and S correction capacitor C8-270nF f 5 percent. If, however, the S correction capacitor is placed between thetwo halves of the secondary, the booster capacitance has to be reduced considerably. (27nF instead of 56nF) because the parabola voltages on C6 and C5 are of opposite sign. Besides, the S correction capacitor has to be reduced (220nF). 7. Marking 8.
